fit: injected isolated caffeine and mouse treadmill endurance
assessment: Caffeine improved mechanical endurance in receptor-expressing mice. No comparable response in the studied knockouts. Injection, mouse endurance and lack of brewed-coffee Parkinson symptoms limit transfer.
The review traces curcumin to laboratory or animal neuroprotection. No consumed ground-turmeric Parkinson pain contrast is given.
Outcome measures concern hippocampal injury and behavior. No frozen Parkinson pain result after eating ground turmeric.

fit: sunflower oil as a nonculinary vehicle in a Parkinson model
assessment: Sunflower oil serves as an injected emulsion vehicle with route and toxin-model differences. No verified cold-pressed oil, direct rigidity measure or clinical oral contrast.

fit: plant constituents in cancer and pathway studies
assessment: The original review links curcumin to turmeric and apigenin to parsley as one of several sources. The relevant outcomes concern neoplastic mechanisms rather than the frozen food-related pain comparisons.

assessment: The test granulate was orange-flavored and placebo had similar taste and appearance. Bowel outcomes follow the probiotic intervention, not a named raw orange ingestion contrast.

fit: string bean questionnaire item and pooled vegetable fatigue association
assessment: Main report gives HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.78–0.88) for total vegetables and the frailty fatigue component. It names string beans in the questionnaire validation. A cooked bean-specific estimate has not been verified and Supplemental Tables 2–3 remain access-pending.
